title: GA readiness checklist for Optimization Config safe apply + rollback (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)

description:

------------------------------
GA READINESS CHECKLIST
------------------------------

A) Scope confirmation (what is GA)
[ ] GA includes: versioned Optimization Config objects + safe apply (validate → staged rollout → promote) + one-click rollback (Console + API), plus audit events + RBAC.
[ ] GA includes Hosted + Dedicated for limited set of accounts; Private is supported with operator procedure (helm/installer/terraform) and docs.
[ ] Out of scope for GA: fully automatic rollback for all customers without human confirmation (allowed only for internal/selected allowlist accounts).
[ ] Confirm current supported optimization surfaces:
    - batching heuristics (runtime scheduling knobs)
    - caching toggles/policies
    - quantization profile selection (gated by eval harness)
[ ] Confirm “blast radius” definitions used in UI and server-side checks:
    - tenant-only (Hosted)
    - tenant + model scope
    - tenant + model + region scope
    - dedicated deployment scope (cluster/pool)
    - private environment scope (namespace/cluster)

B) Feature flags & progressive exposure
[ ] Identify and document all flags and default states (must be off by default for external accounts):
    - OPTCFG_VERSIONING_ENABLED
    - OPTCFG_SAFE_APPLY_ENABLED
    - OPTCFG_CANARY_CONTROLLER_ENABLED
    - OPTCFG_ROLLBACK_ENABLED (Console action + API)
    - OPTCFG_EVAL_GATES_ENABLED (quant-only)
    - OPTCFG_EXPOSE_VERSION_IN_HEADERS (optional; OpenAI compat)
[ ] Confirm kill switch behavior:
    - Flags must immediately prevent new applies/promotes while allowing rollback to proceed.
    - Console rollback button respects server-side authz and cooldown rules.
[ ] Account allowlist management process:
    - Single control plane allowlist source (no duplicated lists in Console).
    - Change to allowlist is audited.
[ ] Release sequencing documented (control plane → runtime → Console), with “safe” intermediate states:
    - If runtime not yet updated, safe apply must refuse to start (clear error) or proceed in “no-op” mode with explicit guard.
    - If Console not updated, API still supports rollback for on-call.

C) Telemetry (metrics, logs, tracing) – minimum viable for GA
[ ] Metrics emitted with required tags: tenant_id, model, region, config_version_id, rollout_id, stage (validate/canary/promote/rollback).
[ ] Gate evaluation telemetry:
    - gate_name (5xx_rate, p95_latency, p99_latency, saturation, eval_quality)
    - decision (pass/fail/timeout/paused)
    - window size + thresholds in event/metric attributes
[ ] Rollout progress metrics:
    - percent_applied, workers_applied/total, shards_applied/total
    - time_to_first_apply, time_to_full_apply, time_to_rollback_complete
[ ] Audit log export validation:
    - audit events include request_id / actor / actor_type / scope / before_version / after_version / reason
    - events are present for create, validate, apply_start, gate_result, pause, resume, promote, rollback_start, rollback_complete
[ ] Console shows the same canonical status as control plane (no derived states that can drift).
[ ] Dashboard exists and is linked from runbook + incident bot:
    - sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/optimization-rollout-health-dashboard.json

D) Dashboards & alerts (SRE readiness)
[ ] Alerts defined for rollout regressions and stuck states:
    - gate_fail (page to on-call only for internal/allowlist during limited GA)
    - rollout_stuck > N minutes (ticket/notify)
    - rollback_failed / rollback_partial (page)
[ ] Alert thresholds reviewed to reduce false positives (especially p95 latency noise):
    - Document default windows + minimum request volume conditions.
[ ] Annotations on graphs for apply/promote/rollback events (to correlate with p95 spikes).
[ ] Error budget gating behavior documented:
    - If global SLO is already burning, safe apply should default to “pause and require explicit override.”

E) Runbooks & operational procedures
[ ] Rollback runbook is complete, reviewed, and tested in gameday:
    - sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/rollback-optimization-config.json
[ ] Safe apply runbook/how-to is complete with examples:
    - sources/confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/apply-optimization-config-with-canary.json
[ ] Dedicated-specific operations:
    - define who is authorized to rollback (customer admin vs Redwood operator) per contract/SLA.
    - confirm “rollback complete” semantics with dedicated pools (worker convergence requirement).
[ ] Private operator procedure documented and validated with at least one internal dry-run:
    - sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/private-deployment-optimization-config-rollback.json
[ ] Incident response hooks:
    - incident-bot shortcut posted (links to dashboard + rollback button + runbook).

F) Security, compliance, and RBAC (launch blockers)
[ ] RBAC roles/permissions finalized and tested:
    - Who can create versions
    - Who can validate
    - Who can apply/promote
    - Who can rollback
    - Who can override gates (internal only at GA)
[ ] Deny-by-default behavior verified:
    - Operators without permissions cannot see/trigger rollback
    - API returns correct error codes and is audited
[ ] Audit log requirements confirmed with Security (field names/retention):
    - sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/optimization-config-audit-events.json
[ ] Data handling confirmations:
    - No sensitive config payload values leaked into logs.
    - Private deployments: audit events available locally; export integration documented.

G) Quality gates for quantization (Applied ML readiness)
[ ] Evals harness gating thresholds finalized for GA for quant profile changes:
    - pass/fail criteria
    - required prompt sets
    - acceptable runtime for canary evals
[ ] Document how we handle noisy eval results:
    - minimum runs / confidence bounds
    - “inconclusive” state behavior (pause + require human decision)
[ ] Rollback restores baseline quality and performance in benchmark-lab validation.

H) Product UX readiness (Console)
[ ] Console history timeline includes: who/what/when, status, scope, and link to diff.
[ ] Diff view highlights “high-risk” fields (batching limits, cache mode, quant profile) and includes a plain-language warning.
[ ] Rollback confirmation modal includes:
    - blast radius summary
    - “type to confirm” for higher blast radius
    - link to dashboard
    - required reason field (audited)
[ ] Partial rollout states are clearly represented (e.g., canary at 10% + paused) and rollback behavior is explicit.

I) Support enablement & customer communications
[ ] Support playbook:
    - How to check active config version
    - How to interpret gate failures
    - When to recommend rollback vs pause vs proceed
[ ] Internal training completed for Support + Solutions Eng (30 min live session + recording).
[ ] Macros/FAQs drafted:
    - “What does rollback change?”
    - “How long does rollback take?”
    - “Why is apply paused?”
[ ] Customer-facing docs published/approved (Hosted/Dedicated) and Private operator guide available.
[ ] Comms plan for limited GA accounts:
    - feature overview
    - what signals are gated
    - expectations on operator involvement

J) Release readiness & test coverage
[ ] E2E tests cover validate → canary → promote → rollback with failure injection (gate fail + worker partial apply + retry).
[ ] Regression coverage for race condition: concurrent apply + rollback cannot result in mixed steady-state.
[ ] Backport plan finalized for any hotfixes during limited GA.
[ ] Release train sequencing confirmed with Connor O'Brien; rollback feature not enabled until runtime+control-plane versions match.

K) Go/No-Go criteria for Limited GA
Must be true for go:
- 100% of audit events present in staging and at least one production internal account.
- Rollback completes successfully within target time for 3 consecutive gameday runs (no manual DB edits).
- Gate evaluation produces <5% false-positive pauses under synthetic steady load.
- Support on-call rotation has access + training; escalation path documented.
- Security sign-off: RBAC verified + audit payload review complete.

No-go triggers:
- Any instance of rollback leaving workers split-brain after convergence window.
- Missing audit event for rollback_complete in production.
- Console presenting “rolled back” while control plane reports “rollback_pending.”

------------------------------
ROLL OUT PLAN (current proposal)
------------------------------
1) Internal beta (Redwood-operated accounts only)
- Enable for internal tenants + perf-canary
- Use to validate gate thresholds and operator UX.

2) Limited GA (Hosted + Dedicated)
- Allowlist 3–5 design partners (include at least 1 quantization-heavy workload)
- Default gates on for 5xx + p95; quant gates required for quant profile changes
- Manual confirmation required for rollback (no automatic rollbacks)

3) Private deployments
- Ship version pinning + rollback procedure as supported feature
- Enable by documentation and operator validation; no automatic gating by default (depends on customer telemetry stack)

------------------------------
OPEN QUESTIONS
------------------------------
- Do we require a “cooldown window” between rollback and a new apply for the same scope (to prevent thrash)? Proposed: 15 minutes; override internal only.
- What is the GA promise for rollback completion time? Proposed: “typically <10 minutes; may vary by fleet size” + show progress in UI.
- For Dedicated: do we allow customer admins to rollback themselves by default, or require Redwood operator role? (Need Sales/CS input.)
